title: Stop Square from breaking Rect's contract

task.text: `Geometry.stretch(Rect)` sets a width of 5 and a height of 4 and expects 20. Pass it a `Square` and it returns 16.
`Square` must stop being usable where a `Rect` is promised. Do not weaken `Rect`: its `setW` and `setH` stay independent. Keep what clients already rely on.

items: `Square(int side)` keeps `area()`, and a `Square` is always square.
Add `interface Shape` with `int area()`, implemented by both `Rect` and `Square`.

checks.title: A Square still reports its area
A Square never breaks the Rect contract
Rect and Square are both Shapes

hints.text: `stretch` relies on a promise made by `Rect`: setting the width leaves the height alone. `Square` cannot keep it, so the problem is the `extends`, not the setters.
Break the subtype link. Put what both really share, `area()`, into `Shape`, and let `Rect` and `Square` each implement it. `Square` keeps its own state and no longer inherits `setW` or `setH`.

lines: class Rect implements Shape { /* as before */ }
public int area() { return side * side; }
